questions.question: According to the principle of dimensional homogeneity, a physical equation is correct when?
options: Both sides have equal numerical values
Dimensions on L.H.S equal dimensions on R.H.S
questions.explanation: The principle of dimensional homogeneity states that for a physical equation to be correct, the dimensions of all terms on the left-hand side must be equal to the dimensions of all terms on the right-hand side.

questions.question: In T = 2π√(l/g), what is the dimension of l/g?
questions.explanation: Length l has dimension [L]. Acceleration due to gravity g has dimension [LT<sup>-2</sup>]. Therefore, l/g has dimension [L]/[LT<sup>-2</sup>] = [T<sup>2</sup>].

questions.question: In the equation T = 2π√(l/g), the constant 2π is?
questions.explanation: 2π is a pure number arising from the geometry of a circle. It has no physical dimensions.

questions.question: The dimension of acceleration due to gravity g is?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. Its dimension is [LT<sup>-2</sup>].

questions.question: Taking the square root of [T<sup>2</sup>] gives?
questions.explanation: The square root of [T<sup>2</sup>] is [T].

questions.question: Since L.H.S = R.H.S = [T], the equation T = 2π√(l/g) is?
questions.explanation: Both sides have the same dimension [T], so the equation is dimensionally homogeneous.

questions.question: Dimensional analysis derives relationships by matching what?
questions.explanation: Dimensional analysis equates the powers of the fundamental dimensions (M, L, T) on both sides of the equation.

questions.question: Frequency f of a stretched string is assumed to depend on length l, tension T, and?
questions.explanation: In the standard derivation, frequency of a stretched string depends on length l, tension T, and mass per unit length μ.

questions.question: In f = k l<sup>a</sup> T<sup>b</sup> μ<sup>c</sup>, k is?
questions.explanation: k is a proportionality constant that has no dimensions.

questions.question: The dimension of frequency f is?
questions.explanation: Frequency is the reciprocal of time, so its dimension is [T<sup>-1</sup>].

questions.question: The dimension of tension T is?
questions.explanation: Tension is a force. Force = mass × acceleration, so [M][LT<sup>-2</sup>] = [MLT<sup>-2</sup>].

questions.question: The dimension of mass per unit length μ is?
questions.explanation: μ = mass / length. Dimension = [M]/[L] = [ML<sup>-1</sup>].

questions.question: Comparing powers of M in [T<sup>-1</sup>] = [M<sup>b+c</sup> L<sup>a+b-c</sup> T<sup>-2b</sup>] gives?
questions.explanation: The left side has no M, so the exponent of M on the right must be zero: b + c = 0.

questions.question: From -2b = -1, the value of b is?
questions.explanation: Solving -2b = -1 gives b = 1/2.

questions.question: Since c = -b and b = 1/2, c equals?
For L, a + b - c = 0. With b = 1/2 and c = -1/2, a equals?
The derived frequency relation is?
questions.explanation: Substituting a = -1, b = 1/2, c = -1/2 into f = k l<sup>a</sup> T<sup>b</sup> μ<sup>c</sup> gives f = k l<sup>-1</sup> T<sup>1/2</sup> μ<sup>-1/2</sup> = k√(T/μ)/l.

questions.question: By finding dimensional formula, one can determine directly the?
questions.explanation: The dimensional formula of a quantity directly gives its S.I. unit.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of coefficient of viscosity η is?
questions.explanation: η = F/(A dv/dx). Dimensions: [MLT<sup>-2</sup>]/([L<sup>2</sup>][T<sup>-1</sup>]) = [ML<sup>-1</sup>T<sup>-1</sup>].

questions.question: In SI, M, L and T are represented by?
questions.explanation: The SI base units are kilogram (kg), metre (m), and second (s).

questions.question: The S.I. unit of coefficient of viscosity is?
questions.explanation: From [ML<sup>-1</sup>T<sup>-1</sup>], the SI unit is kg m<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>.

questions.question: The S.I. unit kg m<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-1</sup> can also be written as?
questions.explanation: 1 Pa = 1 N/m<sup>2</sup> = 1 kg m<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-2</sup>. Therefore, Pa s = kg m<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>.

questions.question: One limitation is that dimensional analysis provides no information about?
questions.explanation: Dimensional analysis cannot determine dimensionless constants or numerical multipliers such as 2π or 1/2.

questions.question: Which can dimensional analysis not determine?
questions.explanation: Dimensional analysis cannot determine whether quantities are added or subtracted in an equation.

questions.question: Dimensional analysis cannot distinguish between different physical quantities that have?
questions.explanation: Different physical quantities can have the same dimensions (e.g., work and torque both have [ML<sup>2</sup>T<sup>-2</sup>]).

questions.question: Dimensional analysis cannot be directly applied to equations containing?
questions.explanation: Trigonometric functions such as sin, cos, and tan cannot be directly analyzed dimensionally.

questions.question: Dimensional analysis cannot be directly applied to equations containing?
questions.explanation: Exponential and logarithmic functions cannot be directly handled by dimensional analysis.

questions.question: Dimensional analysis gives no information about numerical multipliers such as?
questions.explanation: Numerical multipliers like 2π, 1/2, and 3 are dimensionless and cannot be determined by dimensional analysis.

questions.question: Which is NOT a limitation of dimensional analysis?
options: It cannot determine addition or subtraction
questions.explanation: Checking dimensional homogeneity is a strength of dimensional analysis, not a limitation.

questions.question: Dimensional analysis cannot directly handle equations containing?
questions.explanation: Trigonometric functions such as sin, cos, and tan cannot be directly handled.

questions.question: Dimensional analysis cannot directly handle equations containing?
questions.explanation: Logarithmic and exponential functions cannot be directly handled.

questions.question: Dimensional analysis may fail to give a complete relationship because of?
questions.explanation: When several independent variables are present, the relationship derived may be incomplete.

questions.question: Physical quantities are broadly divided into which two categories?
questions.explanation: Physical quantities are classified as scalars and vectors.

questions.question: Which quantity obeys the laws of vector addition?
questions.explanation: Vectors obey the laws of vector addition.

questions.question: A vector possesses?
questions.explanation: A vector has both magnitude and direction.

questions.question: A scalar is a physical quantity that has?
questions.explanation: A scalar has magnitude only.

questions.question: Which is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Mass is a scalar quantity.

questions.question: Which group contains only scalar quantities?
questions.explanation: Mass, time, and temperature are all scalars.

questions.question: Which is an example of a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Work is a scalar quantity.

questions.question: Which is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Displacement is a vector quantity.

questions.question: Which group contains only vector quantities?
questions.explanation: Displacement, velocity, and acceleration are all vectors.

questions.question: Which is NOT a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed is a scalar quantity, not a vector.

questions.question: Which quantity has both magnitude and direction?
questions.explanation: Force has both magnitude and direction.

questions.question: The unit vector i points along the?
questions.explanation: The unit vector i points along the positive x-axis.

questions.question: A unit vector has a magnitude of?
questions.explanation: A unit vector has a magnitude of 1.

questions.question: For a vector A making angle θ with positive x-axis, A<sub>x</sub> equals?
questions.explanation: The x-component of A is A cos θ.

questions.question: For a vector A making angle θ with positive x-axis, A<sub>y</sub> equals?
questions.explanation: The y-component of A is A sin θ.
